Our task is to find $A$ and $B$ such that

$$
\frac{3x+10}{(x+4)(x+5)}=\frac{A}{x+4}+\frac{B}{x+5}.
$$

Multiplying both sides by $(x+4)(x+5)$ gives

$$
3x+10=A(x+5)+B(x+4).
$$

For $x=-4$, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-4)+10 & =A(-4+5)+B(-4+4) \\ -2 & =A \\ A & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=-5,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-5)+10 & =A(-5+5)+B(-5+4) \\ -5 & =-B \\ B & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{3x+10}{(x+4)(x+5)}=\frac{-2}{x+4}+\frac{5}{x+5}.
$$
